headline: Zig’s Governance Is Becoming the Breaking Change
lede: Zig’s technical ambitions are colliding with decisions about stability, contribution, and control. The result is a language whose project governance may now matter as much as its compiler.
pullquote: A language can pursue its vision and still lose the confidence of the people asked to build on it.

headline: Keep SSH Keys Inside the Mac
lede: Apple’s Secure Enclave can hold an SSH private key beyond the reach of disk theft and ordinary malware. Touch ID adds a human gate, but non-exportability turns recovery into an operational responsibility.

headline: A Boeing 737 Lands Beneath a Derbyshire Garden
lede: A retired airliner, a crane, and a hole in the ground become an underground retreat. The hard part is no longer the spectacle of placement, but corrosion, structure, drainage, and planning permission.

headline: The Smart Home Should Survive the Cloud
lede: A dependable home automation system begins with ordinary switches and keeps working when the internet disappears. Local protocols, logs, and graceful fallbacks make convenience something you can maintain rather than merely subscribe to.

headline: 22,000 .name Domains Avoid the Guillotine
lede: A campaign by domain owners and their advocates has preserved existing third-level .name registrations and email redirects. New registrations will close, but long-established online identities will remain in place.

headline: Scion Returns With a Tiny Utility Truck
lede: Toyota’s revived Scion label is testing a fleet-only kei truck with a 660cc engine, four-wheel drive, and a 600-pound payload. The KEI-01 is less a mass-market comeback than a measured experiment in compact mobility.

headline: Ginux Rebuilds the Kernel in User Space
lede: Ginux runs as a Linux process while presenting workloads with a narrower, versioned system contract. It is research software, not a finished sandbox: compatibility, performance, and escape boundaries remain under test.

headline: The 6809 Wins by Turning Its Limits Around
lede: With no graphics acceleration and barely enough cycles to redraw a game, two programmers turned stack operations, register pressure, and tile preprocessing into an advantage. Even memory corruption became part of the rendering plan.

headline: Apple’s Harbor Lines Up Macs for Local AI
lede: A reportedly private-preview Mac app would make serving open-weight models feel more like arranging a studio than configuring a server. Thunderbolt-connected Apple silicon machines could pool memory while keeping prompts and data close to home.

headline: Synthetic DNA Orders Enter the Screening Era
lede: New U.S. rules require federally funded researchers to use approved suppliers that verify customers and screen sequences associated with pathogens and toxins. The policy closes part of the gap between voluntary guidance and a more accessible synthesis technology, while leaving enforcement and coverage questions unresolved.
